fillet.prompt:
Create a production-ready provisional 2D fighting-game pose atlas for the EXACT character in the reference images, preserving identity, face, anatomy, costume, handedness, and weapon silhouettes. First reference is the identity/equipment sheet; second is the existing in-game sprite rendering style. Use crisp black-brown outer contours, thinner interior lines, two-tone hard cel shadows, neutral top-left light, muted local colors with one guild accent. NO redesign, extra limbs, painterly gradients, haze, vignette, ground shadows, impact bursts, text, labels or grid lines. Background MUST be fully transparent alpha=0; character interiors opaque. All eight isolated full-body drawings face screen RIGHT in the same side/three-quarter camera. Exact atlas layout: FOUR equal columns and TWO equal rows, 1536x1024 RGBA PNG, 384x512 cells. Keep each pose, weapons and smears entirely inside its cell with at least 16px transparent separation. Top row WINDUP poses before release, no effects. Bottom row corresponding ACTIVE poses, precisely same model scale and costume as the pose directly above. These are only windup and active frames, not contact or recovery. Keep head size, hand size, clothing landmarks and body proportions consistent across the sheet. Use compact, readable one-crescent slash smears in the accent color with a thin ivory inner edge and at most two trailing wedges; a stab uses a narrow aligned streak. Never obscure the striking hand or blade.
FILLET: short spiky dark-brown hair, red shoulder armor and fitted red corset with brass buckles, ivory shirt and torn ivory apron, charcoal trousers, brown strapped boots, bandaged forearms, TWO curved butcher knives exactly as the reference (not swords). Palette identity crimson #A63242, charcoal #393039, ivory #DDD0B1. Nominal standing body height 310 pixels. Root around x=175, grounded feet at local y=445 in each cell. Never change hair color or apron design between drawings.
Each COLUMN is a different directed action:
Column 1: low traveling KNIFE SPIRAL. Top: deeply crouched loaded stance, both knives pulled beside/behind ribs, coiled hips ready to launch to the right. Bottom: full-body horizontal corkscrew rush traveling RIGHT just above the floor; head and both knife hands lead to the right, boots trail LEFT, body almost horizontal, knees partly tucked to fit. Two real knives clearly lead the attack, a tight pair of crimson crescent ribbons wraps the rotation. It is a spinning knife thrust, NOT a feet-first kick, not a standing spin, not a vertical dive. All anatomy stays recognizable.
Column 2: REKKA FIRST HIT, upward slash. Top: squat with main knife loaded low near the rear hip and the second knife guarding the chest. Bottom: rising diagonal knife sweep from low-left to high-right across the front of her body; front arm and knife extended upward, one thin ascending crimson crescent. This is the first upward attack, not a horizontal swipe.
Column 3: REKKA SECOND HIT, mid stab. Top: planted forward stance, main knife pulled back at the waist, elbow tucked, tip aimed horizontally right. Bottom: firm mid-height horizontal forward knife thrust with a straight lead arm; second knife stays close in guard; narrow crimson motion wedge follows the actual blade, no radial impact.
Column 4: REKKA FINISHER, low slice. Top: compressed low crouch with knife pulled across to the rear, weight on bent rear leg. Bottom: low lunging crouch cutting horizontally across the opponent's shins toward the right, knife and one low crimson crescent close above the ground. Keep this a knife slice, not a leg sweep.

SHARK: lean athletic male, swept-back long white hair, teal eye mask, teal scaled chest armor, asymmetric bone shark-jaw shoulder armor, rope belt and torn teal-and-ivory cloth, gray trousers, brown boots. The main weapon is the long rope-wrapped HOOKED SPEAR/STAFF with the unmistakable curved open metal hook shown in the reference; keep the hook, never turn it into a trident. Other hand retains the short triangular stab blade. Palette slate #34454D, bone #D9D4BD, teal #258A99. Nominal standing body height 270 pixels; root around x=130, feet at local y=445. For hook actives, keep the body slightly left so the entire long diagonal weapon fits to the right. Make the angles clear and EXACTLY about 45 degrees, not horizontal.

Column 1: GROUNDED UPWARD HOOK PULL. Top: both feet grounded, bent knees, torso twisted with hooked spear drawn low behind him, preparing an UP-RIGHT cast/reach. Bottom: quick straight stab with the short blade into mid torso height toward the right; spear held back safely, not crossing the stabbing arm. A small narrow teal stab streak, no impact.
Column 4: AIRBORNE FOLLOW-UP STAB. Top: airborne with tucked knees, short blade drawn back near ribs, hook retracted behind shoulder. Bottom: mid-air horizontal short-blade stab to the right with extended arm, legs remain tucked, hooked staff trails behind without obscuring the body. A small narrow teal stab streak.

prompts.cleanPrompt: Edit this exact Shark eight-pose atlas, keeping its 1536x1024 canvas and four columns by two rows. Preserve the character drawings, proportions, costume, face, palette, placement and rendering style as closely as possible. Make ONE surgical change: in the bottom-left cell and the bottom-row second cell ONLY, remove the long hooked spear completely (shaft, hook and its teal streaks). Retain the hands and their casting/bracing positions, and the short dagger wherever present. Those two poses are the BODY layer for a detached spear projectile that the game will render separately. Their front hand can hold a tiny rope loop but no long line or projectile should be baked into the body. Do not remove the spear from the top-row windups or the bottom-row third/fourth stab poses. These other six poses remain unchanged. Keep each complete character within its own cell and leave clear transparent separation at x384,768,1152. Preserve the reference's distinctive open hook silhouette; do not substitute a spearhead, trident, fishing hook on string, scythe, or extra hooks. Crisp dark contour, hard two-tone cel shadows, neutral upper-left light, matte brown wood, warm tan rope, ivory-gray metal highlights matching the reference. The weapon points diagonally from LOWER LEFT (butt/handle) to UPPER RIGHT (open metal hook), exactly 45 degrees. The whole weapon fits with 100px clear transparent margins on a 1024x1024 RGBA canvas. No shadows, aura, glow, effects, text, labels, grid or other objects. This is a reusable projectile/weapon layer for a 2D fighting game.
